slides.heading: Alphabets Unit – Title
slides.notes: Welcome learners. Today we start the alphabet unit for English class S3 B.

slides.heading: What is an Alphabet?
slides.notes: Explain that an alphabet is a set of symbols representing sounds, essential for reading and writing.

slides.heading: Uppercase Letters
slides.notes: Show examples like Kigali, Rwanda, and discuss why we capitalize the first word of a sentence.

slides.heading: Lowercase Letters
slides.notes: Demonstrate how lowercase letters appear in most of the text we read, e.g., "rwanda".

slides.heading: Sounds of Letters
slides.notes: Pronounce each letter and give simple words like Apple, Banana, and Car to illustrate.

slides.heading: Writing Practice
slides.notes: Students will trace each letter, then write the amount 500 RWF to practice spacing.

slides.heading: Letter Pairs (Digraphs)
slides.notes: Introduce common digraphs with examples such as shy, church, and thank.

slides.heading: Alphabet Song – Rwandan Version
slides.notes: Create a song using A for Akagera, B for Butare, C for Cyangugu, etc., to make learning fun.

slides.heading: Quick Quiz
slides.notes: A short oral quiz to check recognition; ask students to write "Mugisha" with proper capitals.

slides.heading: Summary & Homework
slides.notes: Recap the key points, assign the worksheet, and ask learners to bring five Rwandan words starting with each letter for the next class.
